about: How stage.py compile chooses a video model: the needs code derives from each shot, the first, backup and draft model for each need (blueprint 8.4, C1 §5), how one scene model is chosen, when a shot leaves it, and which picture model makes which picture (C2). Model names are the exact names in video_models.json and image_models.json.

dialogue_recurring.meaning: on-screen dialogue of a recurring speaker: a line whose speaker is seen speaking, sent to the model
dialogue_recurring.first_why: a voice bound to the character keeps it the same in every clip
dialogue_recurring.backup_why: they take the line's recording as an audio reference
dialogue_recurring.marks: V blueprint 8.4; C1 §5 row 1 and R1 [S11][S12][S32][S22]

exact_start_end.meaning: the clip must begin and end on exact pictures

draft.note: first and last pictures only in Google Flow, not in the API

guide_video.meaning: an exact camera path copied from a grey preview video
guide_video.first_why: clay-render reference for camera, pacing and blocking
guide_video.backup_why: copies a camera move from a reference video

long_take.meaning: a held take longer than 15 seconds with its handles: one continuous take, never split

recurring_creature.meaning: a creature (a non-human character) that recurs, built from a reference pack
recurring_creature.first_why: 4-7 reference pictures, each addressed by its tag

physics.meaning: weightlessness or physics a model gets wrong: a guide video, with floating things composited
physics.first_why: with a guide video; floaters composited

wide_establishing.meaning: a wide or extreme wide shot with no dialogue
wide_establishing.marks: V blueprint 8.4; C1 §5 row 3, R15 (native 4K only for wide, detailed shots)

silent_performance.meaning: a close shot (medium close-up or tighter) of a person whose performance carries the beat, with no line sent
silent_performance.first_why: first on the leaderboard without audio
silent_performance.marks: V blueprint 8.4 (row 'silent performance'); C1 §2 [S61]; the reading 'close shot of a person' is J

performance_transfer.meaning: a performance acted on a phone and copied onto the character (route performance_transfer)
performance_transfer.first_why: Motion Control copies body movement and facial expression from a 2 to 5 second clip
performance_transfer.backup_why: performance transfer for up to 8 faces
other_tools: runway-act-two (a 3 to 30 second driving video, about $0.05 a second)
performance_transfer.marks: V C1 §5 row 2, R12 [S78][S80][S28][S36]; not a row of blueprint 8.4's table

need_order_why: when a shot leaves the scene model, the need the scene model cannot meet decides the new model; a length or a guide video is a hard limit, the rest are strengths (J from blueprint 8.4)

default_draft.why: D13 §6.3: draft price $0.05 a second (Veo 3.1 Lite 720p [V])

scene_model.rule: Per scene, one model serves the shots with recurring characters (C1 R14; K29). Each candidate scores, over those shots and each need they have: 2 when the routing names it first for that need, 1 when it names it as backup, 0.5 when it can make the shot but is named for none of its needs, 0 when it cannot. The highest score wins; a tie goes to the cheaper final price.
scene_model.candidates: current video models whose use includes generation and whose status is current (never test_first or retired); with PROJECT licensed_data_only yes, only models marked licensed_data
scene_model.recurring: a CHARACTER whose tier is principal or minor, or who has a VOICE record
scene_model.marks: V blueprint 8.4 and K29 (one scene model, overrides logged with their reason); the points are J

override.rule: A shot leaves the scene model only when the scene model cannot make it: a held take longer than it allows, a start or end picture or guide video it does not take, sound it cannot make for a line that is sent, or too few reference slots. The shot then goes to the first model named for its unmet need that can make it, else the backup, else the cheapest model that can. Every override is logged with its reason, and the pack asks drift questions for it (K29).
override.author_override: SHOT model '<name> | why: ...' wins over routing; a retired name compiles to its first replacement with a warning (blueprint 8.2).

held_take.rule: A held take (a turn shot, a shot in a oner scene, or held: yes) is one clip: if the scene model allows its length with handles, it stays; else it goes whole to a model that allows it (long_take's models); if none does, GEN-10 is an error and the shot is redesigned with a motivated cut. Other shots split only at a planned cutaway, or, as a flagged last resort, chain from the last frame of the clip before.
held_take.marks: V blueprint 8.4; C1 R11; C5 R31

speech.rule: Voices first: every recurring speaker's lines are made as voice takes before any clip with a visible speaking mouth (K16, D3 rule 1). A line whose speaker is seen is sent to the model in its speaker form, with the voice take as an audio reference where the model takes one; a line whose speaker is off screen is laid in during the edit from its voice take and never sent (D3 rule 20). A clip that would carry two speakers seen speaking is made silent and each line is laid in, with lip sync after (C1 R2; D3 §12).
speech.marks: V blueprint 8.6, K16; D3 rules 1, 20, 21; C1 R2

frame_shape.rule: Generate at the first shape the model allows in this list, then crop to the frame shape in finishing; on a 16:9 source for a 2.39 film keep heads, hands and text out of the top and bottom eighths (K24; C1 R23).

resolution.rule: Final takes at the highest of the model's sizes up to 1080p (Seedance 720p, H3 2K), and 4K only where the need row names it (a wide establishing shot); Veo at 720p when the clip is 4 or 6 seconds long, because 1080p forces 8 seconds. Upscale kept takes only after picture lock (D13 R14).
resolution.marks: J from C1 R15, R25; D13 R14

takes.about: [draft takes, final takes] per shot by its cost_class; a still_move shot needs one picture and no clip
takes.marks: V D13 §6.1 (from C3 §17A and C1 R13)

storyboard_named.why: C2 Rule 3: bulk frames with named characters

storyboard_other.why: C2 Rule 3: the cheapest frames without named characters

storyboard_many_characters.why: C2 Rule 4: three or more named characters

end.why: edited from the start picture (C2 Rule 15)

reference.why: C2 Rule 4 and §6.2: five character references

plate.why: C2 R5: empty place, flipped, people added unmirrored with an edit model

still_with_move.why: C1 Ex8: a checked final still, pushed slowly in the editor

pictures.marks: J from C2 Rules 3, 4, 5, 15, 16, 21 and §6.4 [1][2][10][91]; D13 §6.4 (two storyboard tries, about three start-picture tries)
